class.name: NNResponseCurve
class.brief_description: A parametric curve resource for shaping [code]0..1[/code] AI scores.
class.description: A reusable curve resource defined by a preset shape ([enum CurveType]) and tuning parameters rather than hand-placed control points. Assign it to any [code]activation_curve[/code] property, such as [member NNConsideration.activation_curve] or [member NNNQSSearchCriteria.activation_curve]. Use [NNResponseCurve] instead of Godot's [Curve] when you want standard utility AI shapes (linear, polynomial, exponential, S-curve, bell curve, sine, or step) that are quick to adjust with sliders and easy to keep consistent across considerations. Use a regular [Curve] when you need an arbitrary hand-drawn shape.

method.name: sample
method.description: Evaluates the curve at [param x] (clamped to [code]0..1[/code]) and returns a score in [code]0..1[/code].

members.member: The curve shape to evaluate. See [enum CurveType].
Controls how sharply the curve bends. Higher values make the transition steeper (or flatter in the middle for [constant CURVE_LOGIT]). Unused by [constant CURVE_LINEAR] and [constant CURVE_STEP].
If [code]true[/code], flips the output vertically ([code]1.0 - y[/code]) after clamping.
Read-only visual preview of the curve for the inspector.
Vertical scale applied to the curve output before shifting and clamping.
Horizontal offset applied to the input. Positive values shift the curve to the right.
Vertical offset added to the output before clamping to [code]0..1[/code].

constants.constant: An exponential ramp that rises slowly at first and then steeply.
A straight line from [code]0[/code] to [code]1[/code]. Ignores [member exponent].
An S-curve centered at [code]0.5[/code] that transitions smoothly from low to high.
An inverse S-curve that changes quickly near [code]0[/code] and [code]1[/code] and stays flatter through the middle.
A bell curve peaking at [code]0.5[/code], useful for preferring a target value in the middle of a range.
A power curve ([code]x^exponent[/code]). With the default [member exponent] of [code]2.0[/code], it forms a parabola that rises slowly and then accelerates.
A smooth sine hump peaking at [code]0.5[/code] with the default [member exponent] of [code]2.0[/code], or a smooth ease-in-out ramp with [code]1.0[/code].
A hard threshold that outputs [code]0[/code] below [code]0.5[/code] and [code]1[/code] at or above [code]0.5[/code] (shifted by [member x_shift]). Ignores [member exponent].
